title: Count enrolled students and groups by school
user_prompt: Using the students.csv and groups.csv files, how many students are currently enrolled in the program, and how many small-group sessions groups operate at each of the three schools?

gold_facts.claim: The program enrolls 135 students in total.
School SCH-001 has 60 enrolled students.
School SCH-002 has 45 enrolled students.
School SCH-003 has 30 enrolled students.
The program operates 14 tutoring groups across all three schools.
SCH-001 has 6 tutoring groups, SCH-002 has 5, and SCH-003 has 3.

gold_insights: The largest school by enrollment (SCH-001) also carries the most tutoring groups, while the smallest school (SCH-003) has fewer groups proportional to its size.
Eight students (about 5.9% of enrollees) have not yet been assigned to a tutoring group as of the reporting snapshot.
required_limitations: Student counts reflect enrollment as of the snapshot date; students who withdrew before that date are excluded.
Group counts describe the current active roster and do not reflect any mid-quarter reassignments.
forbidden_claims: All enrolled students have been assigned to a tutoring group.
The program operates more than 14 or fewer than 14 groups.
Enrollment figures reflect academic-year cumulative counts.

grounding_accuracy.guidance: Every numeric count must exactly match the rows in students.csv and groups.csv.

insight_quality.guidance: Answer should note the school-size distribution and the unassigned-student gap.

evidence_linkage.guidance: School-level counts must cite the school_id column in students.csv and groups.csv.

calibration_limitation_handling.guidance: Model must not over-generalise beyond the snapshot date.

reference_answer_outline: Report total enrollment (135) broken down by school (60/45/30). Report 14 groups broken down by school (6/5/3). Note 8 students lack a group assignment. Caveat that all figures are point-in-time snapshots.

title: Compute program-wide session attendance rate for the full reporting quarter
user_prompt: Using sessions.csv and attendance.csv, what is the overall student attendance rate across all completed sessions for the full September–November 2025 reporting quarter? Express the result as a percentage rounded to one decimal place.

gold_facts.claim: There are 457 completed sessions across the full quarter.
Across all completed sessions, there are 4156 student-attendance records.
3363 of those 4156 student-attendance records show the student attended.
The program-wide student attendance rate for the quarter is approximately 80.9% (0.8092).

gold_insights: The program's 80.9% quarterly attendance rate narrowly clears the stated goal of 80%, indicating the program is on track but has limited margin.
Computing attendance rate only over completed sessions avoids inflating or deflating the rate by cancelled or no-show sessions.
required_limitations: Attendance is recorded at the student-session level; a student present for part of a session is counted as attended if the tutor recorded the student as present.
Cancelled sessions are excluded from the attendance denominator; including them would substantially lower the computed rate.
forbidden_claims: The attendance rate is computed by dividing completed sessions by total scheduled sessions.
The attendance rate exceeds 85% for the quarter.
All 135 enrolled students have equal numbers of attendance records.

grounding_accuracy.guidance: The 80.9% rate must be derived correctly: attended rows / total rows for completed sessions only.

insight_quality.guidance: Should note proximity to the 80% goal without fabricating causal claims.

evidence_linkage.guidance: Must cite both sessions.csv (to filter to completed) and attendance.csv (for the attended flag).

calibration_limitation_handling.guidance: Must clarify that cancelled sessions are excluded from the denominator.

reference_answer_outline: Step 1: filter sessions.csv to status='completed' (457 sessions). Step 2: join attendance.csv on session_id to get 4156 records. Step 3: count attended=true rows (3363). Step 4: 3363/4156 = 80.9%. Note the goal is 80% and the program is just above it. Mention cancellation exclusion caveat.

title: Retrieve and compare monthly attendance rates across the quarter
user_prompt: Using sessions.csv and attendance.csv, what was the student attendance rate for each month of the reporting period (September, October, and November 2025)? Which month had the lowest rate, and by how many percentage points did it differ from the highest month?

gold_facts.claim: The September 2025 attendance rate across completed sessions is approximately 78.8% (0.7879).
The October 2025 attendance rate across completed sessions is approximately 82.4% (0.8236).
The November 2025 attendance rate across completed sessions is approximately 82.0% (0.8196).
September had the lowest monthly attendance rate (78.8%), and October had the highest (82.4%), a difference of approximately 3.6 percentage points.

gold_insights: Despite October having the highest session-level cancellation rate of the quarter, students who did attend completed sessions in October had a higher attendance rate than in September, suggesting that students with better commitment patterns were the ones attending amid disruptions.
The attendance rate improved from September to October and remained nearly flat through November, indicating a stabilising trend after the program launch.
required_limitations: Monthly rates are computed only over completed sessions; months with more cancellations have fewer sessions in the denominator.
September figures may reflect lower engagement typical of a program launch month rather than a true structural attendance problem.
forbidden_claims: October had the lowest attendance rate.
The attendance rate declined every month across the quarter.
The difference between highest and lowest monthly rates exceeds 10 percentage points.

grounding_accuracy.guidance: All three monthly rates must match the fixture data to within 0.1 pp.

insight_quality.guidance: A strong answer connects October cancellation rate with October attendance rate, noting they measure different things.

evidence_linkage.guidance: Each rate must be attributed to the correct month from sessions.csv.

calibration_limitation_handling.guidance: Must note that cancellation exclusion affects comparability across months.

reference_answer_outline: Filter sessions by month, join attendance, compute attended/total per month: Sep=78.8%, Oct=82.4%, Nov=82.0%. September is lowest, October is highest, gap=3.6 pp. Note September launch-month caveat and October cancellation exclusion.

title: Identify and quantify the October cancellation spike
user_prompt: Using sessions.csv, what was the session cancellation rate in October 2025 — counting sessions that were cancelled (by any party) or resulted in a no-show, out of all scheduled sessions — and how does it compare to September and November? Provide the rate for all three months and the absolute difference (in percentage points) between October and the average of the other two months.

gold_facts.claim: The September 2025 cancellation rate is approximately 10.6% (20 of 188 scheduled sessions were cancelled or no-shows).
The October 2025 cancellation rate is approximately 27.9% (53 of 190 scheduled sessions were cancelled or no-shows).
The November 2025 cancellation rate is approximately 9.5% (16 of 168 scheduled sessions were cancelled or no-shows).
October's cancellation rate (27.9%) is approximately 17.8 percentage points above the average of September and November (10.1%).

gold_insights: October's cancellation rate of 27.9% is roughly 2.8 times the ~10% average of the surrounding months, representing a clear operational disruption rather than typical variance.

Of the 53 October sessions that did not occur, 40 were cancellations (19 student-initiated, 14 tutor-initiated, 7 school-initiated) and 13 were no-shows, suggesting multiple concurrent causes rather than a single root cause.
required_limitations: The cancellation rate is computed as (cancelled + no-show) sessions / all scheduled sessions; it does not account for whether sessions were later rescheduled.
The cancellation categories (cancelled_school, cancelled_student, cancelled_tutor) are self-reported by the recording party and may be inconsistently applied.
forbidden_claims: The October cancellation rate was caused solely by school schedule conflicts.
November had a higher cancellation rate than September.
The overall quarterly cancellation rate exceeded 30%.

grounding_accuracy.guidance: All three monthly cancellation rates and the arithmetic comparison must match fixture data.

insight_quality.guidance: Strong answers break October's non-occurring sessions into cancellations (by type) and no-shows using the status column.

evidence_linkage.guidance: Must cite specific session counts from sessions.csv.

calibration_limitation_handling.guidance: Must note that cancellation type labels are self-reported and rescheduling is unknown.

reference_answer_outline: Count scheduled sessions per month (Sep=188, Oct=190, Nov=168). Count cancelled-or-no-show (Sep=20, Oct=53, Nov=16). Rates: Sep=10.6%, Oct=27.9%, Nov=9.5%. Oct vs avg(Sep,Nov)=10.1%: difference=17.8 pp. Break October's 53 into 40 cancellations (by type) + 13 no-shows. Note rescheduling unknown caveat.

title: Compute the IEP versus non-IEP attendance gap
user_prompt: Using students.csv, sessions.csv, and attendance.csv, compute the student attendance rate separately for students with an Individualized Education Program (IEP) designation and for those without. What is the gap in percentage points between the two groups?

gold_facts.claim: There are 15 students with an IEP designation and 120 students without.
The attendance rate for students with an IEP designation across completed sessions is approximately 68.4% (305 attended out of 446 records).
The attendance rate for students without an IEP designation across completed sessions is approximately 82.4% (3058 attended out of 3710 records).
The gap between non-IEP and IEP attendance rates is approximately 14.0 percentage points.

gold_insights: The 14-percentage-point gap between IEP and non-IEP attendance substantially exceeds the program's stated goal of reducing the gap to 5 percentage points or fewer, signalling a priority area for targeted outreach.
IEP students constitute 11% of enrollment but account for a disproportionate share of absences relative to their group size.
required_limitations: IEP status is a binary flag as recorded in students.csv; it does not capture the type or severity of the students' needs, which may affect attendance patterns differently.
The IEP subgroup is small (15 students), so individual absences by even one or two students can materially shift the computed rate; this figure should be interpreted with caution.
This analysis does not control for school or grade-level effects that may be correlated with IEP status in this cohort.
forbidden_claims: IEP students have the same attendance rate as non-IEP students.
The IEP attendance gap has been closing over the quarter.

grounding_accuracy.guidance: Both subgroup rates and the gap must match the fixture data to within 0.2 pp.

insight_quality.guidance: Should benchmark the gap against the stated program goal of ≤5 pp.

evidence_linkage.guidance: Must show the join logic across all three source files.

calibration_limitation_handling.guidance: Small IEP-group caveat and lack of confound controls must be acknowledged.

reference_answer_outline: Join students.csv (iep flag) → attendance.csv → sessions.csv (filter completed). IEP: 305/446 = 68.4%. Non-IEP: 3058/3710 = 82.4%. Gap = 14.0 pp. Note goal is ≤5 pp, group is small (n=15), and confounders not controlled.

title: Retrieve November 2025 session and attendance metrics as the most-recent complete month
user_prompt: The program director asks for a summary of last month's activity. Assuming the current reporting date is December 1, 2025, use sessions.csv and attendance.csv to report: (a) the total number of sessions scheduled and completed in November 2025, (b) the student attendance rate for completed November sessions, and (c) how November's attendance rate compares to the overall quarter rate.

gold_facts.claim: 168 sessions were scheduled in November 2025.
152 of the 168 November sessions were completed, giving a session completion rate of approximately 90.5%.
The student attendance rate for completed November 2025 sessions is approximately 82.0% (1136 attended out of 1386 attendance records).
November's 82.0% attendance rate is approximately 1.0 percentage point above the full-quarter rate of 80.9%.

gold_insights: November is the strongest attendance month of the quarter, and the program ended the reporting period on an improving trajectory relative to its 80% goal.
Session completion also improved in November: 90.5% of scheduled sessions were completed, compared to 72.1% in October, indicating recovery from the October disruption.
required_limitations: Interpreting November as 'last month' depends on the assumed reporting date; if the reporting date were different, a different month would be current.
A single month's attendance figure may be influenced by end-of-quarter effects such as increased engagement before a break period; it should not be projected forward without additional data.
forbidden_claims: November had the highest cancellation rate of the quarter.
November attendance was below the 80% program goal.
The program completed all 168 scheduled November sessions.

grounding_accuracy.guidance: November scheduled count (168), completed count (152), attendance rate (82.0%), and quarter comparison must all match fixtures.

insight_quality.guidance: Strong answers contextualise November as a recovery month after October's cancellation spike.

evidence_linkage.guidance: Must filter sessions by date range and cite program_context.json for the reporting-period anchor.

calibration_limitation_handling.guidance: Must acknowledge the relative-time interpretation and single-month projection caveat.

reference_answer_outline: Interpret 'last month' as November 2025 given Dec 1 reporting date. sessions.csv: Nov total=168, completed=152. attendance.csv (Nov completed sessions): 1136/1386 = 82.0%. Quarter rate = 80.9%. Gap = +1.0 pp. Note Oct recovery context and single-month caveat.
